$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Resource groups. See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.resourcegroups.rg.crud.title: Resource groups (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.resourcegroups.resources_in_group.title: Resources (every resource type inside the group, at once)

azure.resourcegroups.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to the resource group itself

azure.resourcegroups.deployments.title: Deployments (Microsoft.Resources/deployments) history
limitations: Every resource listed in properties.template.resources is actually created (a real PUT through the same ARM dispatcher, with [parameters('x')] / [variables('y')] resolved to literal values) — but there is no full template-language evaluation: no concat()/resourceId()/reference()/copy-loop support, and dependsOn is not topologically sorted (resources are provisioned in template order). Redeploy re-runs the stored template for real; Cancel honestly 409s, since every deployment here completes synchronously and is never still 'Running' by the time a Cancel call could reach it.

azure.resourcegroups.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill), and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than a real signed-in principal.

azure.resourcegroups.access_control_iam.title: Access control (IAM) — role assignments, roles and checkAccess
limitations: Role assignments are real ARM resources scoped to the resource group they were created under (list + checkAccess only see assignments at or above that scope, same hierarchy inheritance and explicit-deny-wins semantics as the Entra RBAC engine), and the Roles tab + checkAccess cover the built-in Owner/Contributor/Reader/… roles plus any custom role definitions. But checkAccess is a standalone decision tool: no other ARM call in Vyomi consults it, so every other data-plane/control-plane operation still succeeds regardless of what is assigned. Deny assignments and classic administrators are always empty.

azure.resourcegroups.cost_management.title: Cost analysis, budgets and cost alerts, scoped to this resource group

azure.resourcegroups.deploymentstacks.title: Deployment stacks (Microsoft.Resources/deploymentStacks)
limitations: A stack evaluates its ARM template through the same bounded template engine as a plain deployment and OWNS the resources it provisions: deleting the stack deletes them (or detaches them with unmanageAction.Resources=detach), and denySettings.mode denyDelete / denyWriteAndDelete really blocks a direct delete (and write) of a managed resource with 403 DenyAssignmentAuthorizationFailed.

Not modelled: resourceGroups/managementGroups unmanage actions (only resources), deny-settings excludedPrincipals/excludedActions/applyToChildScopes, subscription- and management-group-scope stacks, what-if / validate, and template specs. Template functions beyond the bounded evaluator fail the stack.

azure.resourcegroups.marketplace.title: Creating a new resource from the Marketplace (Vyomi Marketplace)
limitations: Vyomi publishes its own SaaS-simulator offers; subscribing creates a real Microsoft.SaaS/resources resource in this resource group. The third-party vendors' APIs are not emulated and nothing is billed.

azure.resourcegroups.tools.title: Resource group tools: Move resources (validate + move) and Export template
limitations: validateMoveResources / moveResources really re-parent resources inside the one simulated subscription: they check the target group, name clashes, ARM locks, non-movable types and that referenced/referencing resources move together, then rewrite ids and embedded references and re-key state. Moving to another subscription is rejected (Vyomi models one subscription). Real Azure's per-provider move rules (e.g. region/SKU specifics) are approximated by the generic reference-closure check; the call completes synchronously with 204 instead of a 202 long-running operation.

Export template is generated from live state (azure.common export template); dependency-ordered group delete, tag-governance insights and the Tasks tab are not built (Tasks needs an external automation product).
Open query (Azure Resource Graph) and Manage view are separate products/portal chrome and stay not simulated.
